answer: A PoA round commits each eligible identity before a specified future drand quicknet pulse; its threshold-BLS signature then seeds the challenge, so no participant can choose or predict the input in advance. Responses bind the pulse, identity, and task in a commit-reveal proof, making cached answers and offline sybil farming ineffective. The marble, anchor, and gale tasks can vary per pulse; beacon unpredictability raises the cost of automated identities without claiming to prove one person per identity.
